prd_items.note: Content-Length is never copied as a header (FR-PROXY-011 statement and AC-5) and reaches the client only as the relay length (FR-PROXY-014 AC-1).

RFC 9112 §6.3 order (bodyless first, then TE, then CL, then read-until-close) is stated in FR-PROXY-014 Rationale and SEC-PROXY-004 statement; the stricter-than-RFC rejection of non-chunked codings is SEC-PROXY-004 AC-5.

HEAD, 204 and 304 read no body whatever their length headers say (AC-6 covers CL+TE, duplicate, padded, invalid and overflowing CL), matching the PRD note '길이 헤더와 관계없이 본문 없이 끝난 것으로 본다' and the §3.9 table row order.
Single CL read and relayed with that length (AC-1); several equal values read as one (SEC-PROXY-004 AC-7).
Neither header: read until close, relay -1.

Every AC-B16 clause present: statuses 400/404/500, two Set-Cookie, Content-Type, Content-Length and body, hop-by-hop and Connection-listed headers, absent Content-Type, CORS replace plus X-App, three Set-Cookie, Vary both tokens, Trailer removed from a chunked response, FIN-closed early 401.

HEAD keeps the backend Content-Length without a body (FR-PROXY-014 AC-4), 302 relayed not followed (FR-PROXY-011 AC-1), 100 Continue not sent (SEC-PROXY-004 AC-6). A HEAD Content-Length that is not a usable long (AC-6) becomes -1; AC-B17 presupposes a valid length, so this is not a weakening.

srs_items.note: Statement matches the §3.9 response table rows HEAD/204/304, chunked, single CL and neither header; the SEC-PROXY-003 list parsing for the bodyless length agrees with SEC-PROXY-003 statement ('digits that fit in a long and compared numerically'). Links FR-HTTP-036, FR-HTTP-037, FR-PROXY-011, SEC-PROXY-004 and SEC-PROXY-003 all exist and are consistent.
Consistent with FR-PROXY-011 AC-2/AC-5 and FR-HTTP-036 AC-1.
Relay -1 for chunked; consistent with FR-HTTP-037 AC-3.
Client gets Content-Length: 1234 and no body; consistent with FR-HTTP-037 AC-5 (HEAD keeps a non-negative length).

srs_items.basis: fills: PRD-155 / hole / which length a bodyless response passes to relay (design D-058)
srs_items.note: 204 -> -1 and no Content-Length, 304 with CL 10 -> 10, 304 without length -> -1; consistent with FR-HTTP-037 AC-5, AC-6 and AC-9 (relay alone keeps the length on 304). Minimal within PRD-155.

srs_items.basis: PRD-155; fills: PRD-155 / hole / which length relay keeps when the bodyless response carries an unusable Content-Length
srs_items.note: No INVALID_RESPONSE for framing headers of HEAD/204/304 follows PRD-155 and the §3.9 row order; the usable/unusable split uses exactly SEC-PROXY-003's parsing (10 twice and 10/010 -> 10; abc, -1, 20-digit overflow, 10/11 -> -1). Agrees with SEC-PROXY-004 statement, AC-4 and AC-5, which exempt these responses and point back to this criterion. TE is not copied (FR-PROXY-011 hop-by-hop list), so the client sees only the relay framing.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/22.reverse-proxy.srs.md line 1216 (FR-PROXY-014 Implementation Notes): "For a bodyless response, parse `Content-Length` leniently: a single all-digit value or several identical ones gives that length, anything else gives `-1`" vs line 1192 (FR-PROXY-014 AC-6): "a HEAD response and a 304 carrying ... `Content-Length: 99999999999999999999` (beyond `Long.MAX_VALUE`) ... make it call `res.relay` with `-1`" and "the two lines `Content-Length: 10` and `Content-Length: 010` make the proxy call `res.relay` with `10`", and line 1179 (statement): "read with the same list parsing as SEC-PROXY-003 (every element digits that fit in a `long`, elements compared numerically)". A single all-digit 20-digit value 'gives that length' by the note but -1 by AC-6; '010' and '10' are not identical strings yet AC-6 merges them numerically.

findings.description: Round 3 moved the bodyless Content-Length rule to SEC-PROXY-003's list parsing (fits in a long, numeric comparison) but the Implementation Notes still give the older 'single all-digit value or several identical ones' rule, which disagrees with AC-6 on the overflow case and on the numerically-equal-but-textually-different case.

evidence.detail: Request AC-B30 lists '`Content-Length`와 `Transfer-Encoding`을 함께 담은 응답' as giving 502 without naming a status or method, while FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 makes a HEAD/204/304 response with both headers not an INVALID_RESPONSE. The request's own §3.9 table (docs/naruserve-proxy-request.md lines 397-405) orders the row 'HEAD 요청에 대한 응답, 204, 304 — 본문을 읽지 않음' before the TE+CL row, under 'RFC 9112 §6.3의 순서대로'.

findings.description: Not a contradiction: AC-B30 is an example list satisfiable by a GET 200 test, which SEC-PROXY-004 AC-4 requires, and the request's §3.9 table explicitly puts the bodyless row first.

evidence.detail: FR-PROXY-014 AC-4: 'the client receives `Content-Length: 1234` and no body well before the read timeout'.

findings.description: 'well before' is soft, but the criterion is decidable: a proxy that read body bytes from a kept-open backend would block until the read timeout and then fail, so a test asserting completion before the configured read timeout distinguishes the two. No deterministic defect.

evidence.detail: `ls NaruServe-proxy` -> 'No such file or directory'; the Code trace row carries trace_intent=addition_site.

findings.description: The path is a declared addition site for a new module, so its absence is expected.

evidence.detail: Design D-058 (docs/research/naruserve-proxy/design/00.design.md line 116): 'The proxy SHALL validate the framing headers of every response before skipping the body of a HEAD, 204 or 304 response'. FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 does not validate them.

findings.description: The design only decides defaults for gaps; the request's §3.9 row order and PRD-155 ('길이 헤더와 관계없이') decide this point, and FR-PROXY-014 Implementation Notes record the precedence and keep D-058's length choice. Not a defect.
